acceptance: Cloud readings are joined and isolated: views asking at once share one flight, a snapshot belongs to one account namespace (user, session generation, API) and another account clears every snapshot and cancels the old flights, so a late answer of the old one never lands. Readings are fresh for 30 s and stay readable while stale for one background revalidation; caches are bounded by entries, and file bodies are never cached. A change drops only the listings it names (the parent and the subtree), an unrelated read in flight stays shared, and a read a change superseded is read again rather than cached; mutations through the workspace invalidate their listings and a lease that ends leaves nothing behind.

A stalled billing read ends within the transport's bounded budget and its request is dropped. Resolving a repository context is a read and leaves file listings alone; workspace mutations invalidate theirs. Billing goes only to the BFF's organization routes (quote, checkout, plan change, seat change) with each intent's idempotency key and the product's bodies; an unsafe organization id is never sent. A billing catalog of another schema major or carrying the provider's private data is refused (the current catalog has no overage switch to check). Only a safe checkout URL may open in the system browser. A new Cloud Project is created in the chosen Space as the publish contract defines, keyed by its operation so a retry is the same request. Project settings are trimmed into one PUT and an empty update or blank name is refused unsent. History reads 80 summaries per page by the topological contract and cursor, normalizes legacy optional fields, and fails closed on another project, missing topology or inconsistent pagination. Errors keep their status, allowlisted code, retry decision and request id; a request under a lease of another API base is refused before it is sent. The default Space falls back to the personal route only when the new route is absent, and provisioning is never retried after 401, 403, 409 or 500.

reason: TS v0.4.4 validates its billing summary, quote and operation shapes strictly: a closed summary status set, required seat_changes_available and runtime unit fields, a closed application_mode set and consistent lifecycle flags. The native client reads the current billing service's contract (allowances, add-ons, pending seat changes) and checks what it acts on: organization identity, schema major 1, unique plans, no private provider data, safe URLs, that a quote and its operation answer the request, and that what was seen to end stays ended. Statuses, modes and flags it does not act on are read leniently rather than refused.

TS percent-encodes an organization or project id that contains '/' into one path segment (org%2F1, a%2Fb) and reads an organization's seat usage for the team details of its initialization route. The native client refuses an identifier that is not a single safe path segment before sending anything (Cloud issues no such ids), and its first publication chooses a Space without reading seat usage.
